skills.title: Paper → reproduction benchmark. Functional-assay calibration to ACMG/AMP evidence — clean-room reimpl of rosstewart/exCALIBR (Zeiberg et al. bioRxiv 2025). Bootstrap constrained skew-normal mixture EM + Bayesian (Tavtigian) calibration turns MAVE / VAMP-seq / SGE scores into PS3 / BS3 evidence strengths. Subcommands: thresholds, prepare, run, assign, selftest.
skills.summary: exCALIBR — functional-assay calibration to ACMG/AMP evidence (IGVFagent port).

tools.name: calibrate_assign
tools.description: Apply an existing calibration to a table of assay scores: each score gets its evidence point value and the ACMG/AMP criterion + strength it supports (e.g. 'PS3 moderate', 'BS3 strong', 'no evidence'). USE THIS after calibrate_run, or with a published calibration JSON, to interpret new variants.

calibration.description: Path to a *_calibration.json from calibrate run.

scores.description: CSV/TSV with a score column (plus any ID columns).

tools.name: calibrate_prepare
tools.description: Build the score/sample input table a calibration needs. Labels variants into the four calibration samples — 0 P/LP and 1 B/LB from ClinVar (with a review-star quality gate), 2 population from gnomAD membership, 3 synonymous — from an IGVF / Pillar-format scoreset (`pillar`), a plain score/sample CSV (`table`), or a `mavedb map-scoreset` output joined to ClinVar (`mapped` + `clinvar_tsv`). Reports the per-sample counts so you can see whether the scoreset has enough labelled variants to calibrate at all.

mapped.description: mavedb map-scoreset output with chr/pos/ref/alt + score.

tools.name: calibrate_run
tools.description: CALIBRATE A FUNCTIONAL ASSAY TO ACMG/AMP EVIDENCE ★. Full exCALIBR chain (Zeiberg et al. 2025) on a variant-effect scoreset: bootstrap constrained skew-normal mixture EM over the P/LP, B/LB, gnomAD-population and synonymous samples → EM prior → LR+(score) → Tavtigian C → the score window that earns each evidence strength (PS3 / BS3 supporting → very strong), plus 2c-vs-3c model selection, a calibration JSON and a figure. Input is either an IGVF / Pillar-format scoreset CSV (`pillar`) or a score/sample table from calibrate prepare (`table`). LONG JOB: runs to completion in one call with a progress heartbeat and a resumable ledger — lower `n_bootstraps` / `fits_per_bootstrap` for a quick look (defaults 1000 x 100 are the paper's settings).

pillar.description: Path to an IGVF / Pillar-format scoreset CSV (carries auth_reported_score + ClinVar + gnomAD + SpliceAI).

table.description: Path to a score/sample CSV (from calibrate prepare).

name.description: Dataset name; also selects one Dataset from a multi-dataset Pillar table.

tools.name: calibrate_thresholds
tools.description: ACMG/AMP EVIDENCE THRESHOLDS FROM A PRIOR ★. Solves Tavtigian's constant C (O_PVSt) for a given prior probability of pathogenicity and prints the likelihood-ratio (LR+) threshold for every evidence strength — supporting / moderate / strong / very strong, on both the PS3 (pathogenic) and BS3 (benign) sides. Instant, no data or fitting needed. USE THIS to answer 'how strong must an assay LR+ be to count as PS3 moderate?' or to sanity-check a published calibration.

prior.description: P(pathogenic) in the reference population, e.g. 0.1 for a well-studied disease gene, 0.01 for a low-prior gene.

point_values.description: Comma list of evidence point values (default 1..8).

It is REJECTED if the --cli subcommand does not exist, because such a tool registers cleanly and then fails on every call. **If the capability does not exist yet, use ext_author_skill instead** — it writes the implementation AND registers the tool in one step. skills.title: Gene regulatory network (dEx) + protein-variant effects from the Catalog

tools.name: grn_network
tools.description: Differential-expression gene regulatory network (dEx GRN) edges from the IGVF Catalog. Call this for 'what genes does TF X regulate?', 'what regulates gene Y?', 'is there a Perturb-seq self-edge for TF Z?', or any question about regulator->target effect size or significance. Returns one row per element->gene edge with log2FC, neg_log10_pvalue, significant, crispr_modality and the perturbed element's coordinates. Query from either end: 'regulator' gives that TF's targets, 'response' gives that gene's regulators, and passing BOTH with the same symbol tests the self-edge (many TFs legitimately have none). This is the only tool that reaches /api/gene-regulatory-network — kg_gene and catalog_find_associations do not cover it.

regulator.description: Regulator (TF) gene symbol; returns its targets. e.g. EOMES

response.description: Response gene symbol; returns its regulators. e.g. ARHGEF3

method.description: Assay method: 'Perturb-seq' or 'CRISPR screen'. Omit for all methods.

p_value.description: Keep edges with p <= this (typical: 0.05). Omit to return all edges regardless of significance.

host.description: 'dev' queries the pre-release demo Catalog; use only when the user explicitly asks for dev data.

tools.name: grn_protein_variants
tools.description: Sequence-variant effects on proteins from the IGVF Catalog: allele-specific binding and motif-disruption calls (SEMVAR, ADASTRA). Use for 'which variants alter binding of TF X?' or 'what is the allele-specific binding evidence for this protein?'. Returns sequence_variant, protein_complex, biosample_term, the effect label (e.g. 'allele-specific binding' / 'binding modulated by'), method and source_url. skills.title: MPRA / STARR / BlueSTARR retrieval and analysis

tools.name: mpra_activity
tools.description: Per-oligo MPRA activity: negative-binomial GLM Wald test (DESeq2 via pydeseq2) of RNA vs DNA counts, followed by summit-shift normalization that moves the mode of the log2-fold-change density to zero (Tewhey-lab MPRAmodel convention). Emits a .out table with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj per Oligo. Input: a counts table with an 'Oligo' column and DNA_*/RNA_* replicate columns; barcode-level tables (with a 'Barcode' column) are summed per oligo automatically.

tools.name: mpra_pull
tools.description: Pull MPRA/STARR/BlueSTARR metadata from Catalog or Portal. Backed by /api/variants/biosamples, where the reporter assay is carried by the Catalog 'method' field: 'STARR-seq' for the measured assay and 'BlueSTARR' for the neural-network predictions over it (source='IGVF'). Those are distinct record sets — say which one the user means rather than conflating them. This collection is region-queryable (e.g. chr4:155600-155770).

tools.name: mpra_qc
tools.description: MPRA QC suite: replicate concordance (pairwise Pearson r on log10 counts, separately for DNA and RNA, with an N x N SVG heatmap), unique-barcodes-per-oligo histogram (when a 'Barcode' column is present), and total-counts-per-oligo histogram (log10). Writes a markdown QC report alongside the SVGs.

tools.name: mpra_skew
tools.description: Allelic-skew analysis: pairs ref/alt oligos by SNP_window_strand_haplotype, computes per-replicate log2((RNA+1)/(mean DNA+1)) for each allele, runs a paired t-test of alt vs ref across replicates, and applies BH-FDR. Emits a .out table with Log2Skew, LogSkew_SE, tstat, pvalue, padj per element. Mirrors the t-test path of Tewhey-lab MPRAmodel runSkew.

input.description: Counts table with Allele plus at least one of SNP/Window/Strand/Haplotype.

tools.name: mpra_volcano
tools.description: Render a 4-panel volcano figure (activity volcano, allelic-skew volcano, activity MA plot, skew MA plot) from the .out tables produced by `mpra activity` and `mpra skew`. Points with padj below the FDR threshold are highlighted in red.

skills.title: 10x Multiome retrieval pipeline

tools.name: multiome_atac_spectral
tools.description: Jaccard-Laplacian spectral embedding alternative to LSI for ATAC peak matrices (snapATAC2-style). Robust to depth differences without explicit depth-correction drop. Good for datasets where TF-IDF + LSI gives a strong depth axis.

tools.name: multiome_chromvar
tools.description: Clean-room chromVAR-style TF motif activity per cell. For each (cell, motif) pair, computes raw deviations from expected accessibility, then bias-corrects via K=50 GC-content + log-mean-accessibility-matched background motif sets, yielding a per-cell z-score for every motif. Output: cells × motifs z-score TSV.

tools.name: multiome_css
tools.description: Cluster Similarity Spectrum batch correction (He 2020 Genome Biol). Per-batch HVG → per-batch Leiden → per-batch cluster centroids → represent each cell as its vector of correlations to all batch×cluster centroids. Apache/BSD-friendly alternative to GPL Harmony.

tools.name: multiome_da_peaks
tools.description: Differential accessibility on TF-IDF-normalized peaks via Wilcoxon rank-genes. Pairs naturally with peak2gene — peak2gene gives enhancer→gene candidates; da-peaks tells you WHICH peaks are differentially open between user-defined clusters / cell-types.

input.description: ATAC h5ad (peaks will be TF-IDF normalized).

tools.name: multiome_joint_qc
tools.description: Merge ATAC + RNA per-barcode QC tables and apply Signac-convention joint thresholds (RNA: 1k-25k UMIs, ≥200 genes, ≤20%% MT; ATAC: 1.8k-100k frags, TSS>1, nucleosome<2, FRIP>0.15). Outputs a per-barcode QC TSV with 'qc' label (both / RNA only / ATAC only / neither).

tools.name: multiome_lsi
tools.description: TF-IDF normalization + truncated SVD on a peak × cell matrix. Drops dim 1 (correlates with sequencing depth) per Signac RunSVD + DepthCor convention. Writes the embedding to obsm['X_lsi'] of the input h5ad and saves a new h5ad.

tools.name: multiome_multivi
tools.description: MultiVI deep joint VAE (Ashuach 2023) via scvi-tools. Optional dep — install with `pip install scvi-tools` to enable. Joint generative model over RNA (ZINB) + ATAC (Bernoulli on binarized peaks) yielding a shared latent z, with batch-key-conditioned encoder/decoder.

tools.name: multiome_peak2gene
tools.description: Peak-to-gene correlation. For each peak, identify genes whose TSS is within --window bp (default 500 kb) and compute Pearson/Spearman correlation between peak accessibility and gene expression across cells. BH-FDR adjusted p-values. Sign of correlation indicates enhancer-like (positive) vs repressor-like (negative) association.

tools.name: multiome_qc_atac
tools.description: Per-barcode ATAC QC from a fragments TSV/BED ★. Computes fragments per barcode, TSS enrichment (Signac TSSEnrichment formula: center reads / max(0.2, flank reads), ±100 bp center / ±900-1000 bp flank), nucleosome signal (mono-nucleosome / NFR fragment-length ratio), and FRIP (reads in peaks). Use this BEFORE joint-qc.

tss_bed.description: Optional TSS BED for TSS enrichment.

tools.name: multiome_retrieve
tools.description: Discover IGVF 10x Multiome AnalysisSets; writes file/sample/donor manifest.

tools.name: multiome_showcase
tools.description: ONE-COMMAND 10x MULTIOME QC SHOWCASE ★. Runs qc-atac + (optional) joint-qc + builds a 6-panel composite figure (fragments/cell, TSS enrichment, nucleosome signal, FRIP, reads in TSS, reads in peaks — each with Signac thresholds as red dashed lines) + writes a narrative report. THIS IS THE RIGHT TOOL FOR ANY 10x MULTIOME QC DEMO QUESTION.

rna_qc.description: Optional RNA QC TSV (output of share rna-qc).

tools.name: multiome_wnn
tools.description: Joint weighted-nearest-neighbor embedding via muon (BSD-3). Equivalent to Seurat 5 FindMultiModalNeighbors. Requires both AnnData inputs to share per-cell barcodes; ATAC must have obsm['X_lsi'] (run `multiome lsi` first). Optionally clusters the joint graph with Leiden.

tools.name: portal_batch_download
tools.description: IGVF PORTAL BATCH-DOWNLOAD MANIFEST ★. Hits `/batch-download/` for a FileSet type (MeasurementSet / AnalysisSet / etc.) and returns a manifest of pre-signed S3 URLs for every File hanging off the selected sets. Optional `fetch=true` actually pulls each file to disk. USE THIS to grab raw data files for a slice of IGVF in one round-trip.

tools.name: portal_endpoint_params
tools.description: IGVF PORTAL ENDPOINT-PARAM INTROSPECTION (the DACC UX trick) ★. For any portal collection (`measurement-sets`, `analysis-sets`, `sequence-files`, ...), returns the documented filter set as a table mapping the Python-friendly snake_case `agent_param` (file_set_id, lab_title, samples_taxa, ...) to the dotted `search_field` the search index understands (file_set.@id, lab.title, samples.taxa, ...). Lets an LLM pivot between tooled and raw search without re-learning fields.

tools.name: portal_facets
tools.description: IGVF PORTAL FACETS-ONLY CALL ★. Calls `/search/` with `limit=0` to retrieve only the `facets[]` aggregation block — no items, just per-category value counts (assay titles, lab ids, taxa, sample terms, perturbation modality, file formats, etc.). USE THIS to summarise what IGVF has across a slice of data (e.g. 'how many of each assay class for human putamen tissue?'). Set `field` to the name of ONE facet (e.g. 'content_type') to dump EVERY value of that facet with counts instead of the top-5 preview — the reliable way to discover the exact filter term for a rare value in a single call, rather than guessing field_filters and getting 404s.

tools.name: portal_get

Resolves a single item by @id ('/measurement-sets/IGVFDS3909HJKS/'), accession ('IGVFDS3909HJKS'), or UUID, returning the full embedded JSON + @type breakdown + saved file. USE THIS to inspect a specific MeasurementSet / AnalysisSet / Donor / etc. that you know the id of.

tools.description: List the canonical IGVF CamelCase ItemTypes and their snake-case collection paths (e.g. MeasurementSet ↔ /measurement-sets/). Useful as a quick lookup before calling portal_search or portal_schema.

tools.name: portal_report
tools.description: IGVF PORTAL TSV REPORT EXPORT ★. Streams the canonical `/report.tsv` export for an ItemType (paginated server-side) to disk. Returns row + column count + first-8-column preview + saved TSV path. USE THIS when you need a spreadsheet-shaped dump of every matching item (lab inventories, file manifests, donor cohorts) rather than the per-item JSON.

tools.name: portal_schema
tools.description: IGVF JSON SCHEMA INTROSPECTION ★. Fetches the canonical JSON schema (`/profiles/<Type>.json`) for any CamelCase ItemType (MeasurementSet, SequenceFile, HumanDonor, etc.) and reports title + description + all 60+ documented properties. USE THIS to discover what fields exist on a type before constructing a search / report query.

tools.name: portal_search
tools.description: IGVF PORTAL FACETED SEARCH (canonical DACC pattern) ★. Searches the IGVF Portal `/search/` endpoint with a typed ItemType filter (MeasurementSet / AnalysisSet / SequenceFile / HumanDonor / etc.) and an optional free-text query, returning matching `@graph` items + total count + saved JSON. Supports the DACC field-filter DSL: dotted embedded fields (`lab.@id=/labs/x`), negation (`field!=val`), range ops (`gte:`/`lte:`/`gt:`/`lt:`), and list values (`field=a,b,c`). Clauses joined by `;`. USE THIS for any 'find me IGVF Portal items where ...' question. Works anonymously over `api.data.igvf.org` for released items; HTTP Basic auth via IGVF_ACCESS_KEY/SECRET unlocks restricted ones.

tools.description: Recommend a study workflow + cognate published studies + matching IGVF Portal AnalysisSets for an assay type.

tools.name: ref_learn
tools.description: Multi-source literature search (PubMed/bioRxiv/arXiv/SemanticScholar/OpenAlex). Ranks by journal+citations; extracts methods + plot vocabulary; emits a consensus figure recipe.

tools.name: ref_validate
tools.description: Cross-check a CSV of genes/variants/regulatory elements against prior literature.

skills.title: Bulk RNA-seq QC / PCA / DEG / DEG→cCRE linkage

tools.name: rnaseq_link_cre
tools.description: Given a DEG CSV (with `gene`, `log2FC`, `padj` columns), query the IGVF Catalog for the regulatory elements that control each significant gene. Useful as a follow-up to an existing DEG analysis.

tools.name: rnaseq_pipeline
tools.description: End-to-end bulk RNA-seq: QC + PCA + differential expression (pyDESeq2 if installed, Welch's t-test + BH FDR fallback) + volcano/MA/heatmap plots + DEG → controlling cCRE linkage via the IGVF Catalog. Inputs: counts matrix + sample sheet + two group labels in --condition-col.

skills.title: Single-cell analysis: QC, PCA, UMAP, t-SNE, Leiden, markers, publication figures (Scanpy-driven)
skills.summary: Single-cell analysis skill — UMAP / t-SNE / clustering / markers.

tools.name: sc_cluster
tools.description: Leiden clustering on the k-NN graph (falls back to Louvain if leidenalg missing). Saves UMAP colored by leiden cluster.

tools.name: sc_pipeline
tools.description: Full single-cell analysis pipeline: QC + filter, log-normalize, HVG selection, PCA, k-NN graph, UMAP, t-SNE, Leiden clustering, and marker-gene DE. Accepts .h5ad / 10x .h5 / .mtx / .csv / .tsv. Saves processed.h5ad, markers.csv, and publication PNGs (UMAP colored by cluster / sample / top markers). The headline tool when a user asks for a UMAP / t-SNE / cluster analysis.

sample_col.description: Obs column to color UMAP by (sample, batch).

tools.name: sc_plot_embedding
tools.description: Re-render UMAP or t-SNE coloured by any combination of obs columns and/or gene symbols. Use when the user asks 'show me APOE on the UMAP we just made' or wants a sample/batch overlay.

tools.name: sc_qc
tools.description: Standalone QC pass: load counts, filter cells (min-genes), filter genes (min-cells), drop high-mito cells, write QC violins, save a cleaned processed.h5ad. Use when the user wants QC numbers before committing to a full pipeline run.

tools.name: sc_umap
tools.description: Run k-NN + UMAP on an already-PCA'd anndata, write a UMAP figure colored by clusters (if present) or QC. Skips PCA if X_pca exists.

validation.scope_note: Benchmarks execute fixed command sequences with no model in the loop, so this establishes implementation correctness only — not that an agent would select this skill unaided. See Docs/EVALUATION.md.

skills.title: scE2G element→gene linkages → local KG (bulk, adaptive region tiling, resumable, runs to completion regardless of size)
skills.summary: scE2G → local Knowledge Graph bulk ingestion.

tools.name: sce2g_kg_pull
tools.description: BULK-ingest scE2G element→gene regulatory linkages from the IGVF Catalog into the local KG as `regulates` edges. Deterministic, resumable, runs to completion over the whole genome regardless of size (adaptive region tiling around the API's 500-row cap) with a progress heartbeat. USE THIS for 'download/integrate all scE2G linkages' — one call, not a per-gene loop. Scope with `region` (default 'all' = whole genome) or `chromosomes`.

region.description: 'all' (whole genome, default), a chromosome ('chr19'), or a locus ('chr19:44900000-45000000').

skills.title: scEPS single-cell disease-neighborhood statistics — clean-room reimpl of Genentech/sceps. Integrates GWAS (MAGMA Z) + single-cell atlas; per-neighborhood variance-component d-statistic (GWAS vs matched control genes). Subcommands: estimate. Runs under the scEPS env (scanpy/anndata/statsmodels).
skills.summary: scEPS — single-cell Expression exPlainability Statistics (IGVFagent port).

skills.title: Super-enhancer → target-gene pipeline (ENCODE)

tools.name: se_targets_discover
tools.description: List candidate ChIP-seq + DNase/ATAC + Hi-C/ChIA-PET experiments for a biosample without downloading or analyzing anything. Use this to scope what's available before running the full pipeline.

tools.name: se_targets_pipeline
tools.description: End-to-end super-enhancer → target-gene pipeline. For a chosen biosample (GM12878 / K562 / HepG2 / liver / brain / ...): discovers H3K27ac (or BRD4/MED1/P300) ChIP-seq + optional Hi-C/ChIA-PET 3D experiments, downloads peak BED, calls super-enhancers ROSE-style, and links each SE to candidate target genes via four streams (3D loops, IGVF Catalog rE2G/ABC predictions, proximity, SCREEN cCRE composition). Outputs a ranked SE↔gene table, network plot, and report.

biosample.description: ENCODE biosample term (GM12878, K562, liver, hippocampus, ...).

gene.description: Optional gene to focus a per-locus browser view on.

skills.title: SHARE-seq joint scATAC+scRNA QC (Ma 2020 / Broad pipeline)

tools.name: share_demultiplex_bcs
tools.description: SHARE-seq round-1/2/3 24-mer barcode demultiplex on a gz FASTQ. Exact match + 1-Hamming-mismatch lookup + optional +/-1 bp shift correction. Pure stdlib; no pysam/dnaio. Mirrors correct_fastq.py from broadinstitute/epi-SHARE-seq-pipeline.

tools.name: share_fragment_qc
tools.description: Per-barcode ATAC QC from a SHARE-seq fragments BED: total fragments, reads in TSS +/-2kb window, reads in flanking 100bp regions, TSS enrichment (Ma 2020 formula with 0.2 floor), reads in peaks, FRIP. Mirrors qc_atac_compute_tss_enrichment.py + qc_atac_compute_reads_in_peaks.py.

tools.name: share_joint_qc
tools.description: Merge SHARE-seq RNA + ATAC per-barcode tables and apply the Ma 2020 joint cell-calling thresholds (UMIs>=min_umis AND genes>=min_genes AND TSS>=min_tss AND fragments>=min_frags). Mirrors joint_cell_plotting.py.

tools.name: share_multiplet_detect
tools.description: Pairwise Jaccard multiplet detection on a SHARE-seq fragments BED. Builds a per-barcode set of (chrom, start) coordinates, samples a null Jaccard distribution from 10000 random pairs, and flags any pair whose Jaccard exceeds the 99-th percentile of null. Mirrors detect_multiplets.py.

tools.name: share_pull_portal
tools.description: Discover IGVF Portal SHARE-seq AnalysisSets and MeasurementSets (`preferred_assay_titles=SHARE-seq`). Writes a TSV manifest covering both processed AnalysisSets (h5ad + fragments BED) and raw MeasurementSets (FASTQ + seqspec).

tools.name: share_rna_qc
tools.description: Per-barcode RNA QC from a SHARE-seq h5ad sparse gene-count matrix: total UMIs, expressed genes, percent mitochondrial (genes auto-detected by MT-/mt- prefix).

skills.title: STARR-seq allelic test (mpralm clean-room rewrite)

tools.name: starr_activity
tools.description: Per-fragment STARR-seq log activity = log(RNA TPM / DNA TPM) across paired replicates, plus per-SNP allelic skew (log activity ALT - REF).

tools.name: starr_aggregate
tools.description: Collapse barcode-level STARR-seq counts to a per-(SNP, Allele) wide table (long form -> wide).

tools.name: starr_allelic_test
tools.description: STARR-seq allelic significance test: per-(SNP, Allele) OLS on log2((RNA+0.5)/(DNA+0.5)) per replicate, eBayes variance moderation (Smyth 2004 trigamma inversion) with graceful fallback when no variance excess is detected, BH-FDR. Clean-room rewrite of Bioconductor mpra::mpralm.

tools.name: starr_pull_portal
tools.description: Discover IGVF Portal STARR-seq MeasurementSets. Writes a TSV manifest with accession, assay_titles, n_files, status.

tools.name: starr_qc
tools.description: STARR-seq counts QC: TPM-style scaling, low-expression filter, RLE matrix, per-sample Spearman D-statistic outlier flag (top 5%). Mirrors count_qc.R from gaochengwen/STARR-seq-Data-Analysis.

skills.title: Annotate variants against IGVF Catalog evidence

tools.name: annotate_variants
tools.description: Annotate a variant CSV against IGVF Catalog evidence (CADD/QTL/phenotypes/regulatory). CSV needs rsid/hgvs/spdi or chr/pos/ref/alt.

skills.title: Annotate a pasted/file variant list in any notation (chr-pos-ref-alt, rsID, SPDI, HGVS, VCF) via FAVOR + IGVF Catalog, and add the results to the local KG
skills.summary: Annotate a variant list in any common notation, and land it in the KG.

tools.name: annotate_variant_list
tools.description: ANNOTATE A LIST OF VARIANTS PASTED BY THE USER ★ and add them to the local knowledge graph as variant vertices. Pass the list VERBATIM in `variants` — any notation and any separator works (2-21001846-G-A, chr2:21001846:G:A, rs763341676, SPDI, HGVS, VCF lines; spaces, commas or newlines). THIS IS THE RIGHT TOOL whenever someone pastes variants and asks to annotate, characterise, or add them to the KG — do NOT ask them for a CSV file first. Queries FAVOR (CADD, ClinVar, GENCODE, enhancer/promoter overlap) and the IGVF Catalog, writes a report plus CSV/JSON, and upserts variant nodes with edges to genes and diseases.

variants.description: The variant list verbatim, any notation.

input.description: Alternative: path to a file of variants.

label.description: Short label for the run directory.

no_kg.description: Annotate without writing to the KG.
